executive.summary: Eight illustrative workflows show the operating shape leadership needs to review: ownership is incomplete, delivery evidence is stronger than use evidence, and no value claim has a validated manual baseline yet.

narrativeCards.title: What changed
narrativeCards.body: Two repeatable workflows now have a confirmed trigger and maintenance path. Their maturity improved, but outcome evidence did not change.

narrativeCards.title: Evidence of value
narrativeCards.body: One workflow has documented use and three have delivery evidence. None has an owner-approved baseline, so capacity and ROI remain unclaimed.

narrativeCards.title: Decision required
narrativeCards.body: Leadership should assign owners to three workflows and decide whether outcome instrumentation is worth adding to the weekly operating review.

methodology.sourceCoverageSummary: Two illustrative local inventory sources are represented. Live identity and outcome evidence are intentionally unavailable in this sample.
methodology.evidenceBoundary: Executed, delivered, consumed, used, outcome linked, and validated value remain separate. A workflow that only delivered is described as: Delivered successfully. Usefulness not yet verified.
methodology.methodology: The unit is a meaningful workflow. Inventory records are evidence inputs, not automatic workflows. Maturity reflects operating structure and is assigned only when every requirement for a level is met.
methodology.privacy: Team-level aggregation is the default. Person-level ownership requires authorization and confirmed identity. Raw conversations, sensitive source content, and people leaderboards are excluded.
